subject: literature
passage: For thirty-one years, Teodor Vasile had walked the aisles of the night train from the capital to the coast, and on his final run he moved more slowly than usual, as though memorizing each worn seat. Near dawn, a young passenger looked up from her book and asked whether the train was always so quiet. "Not ______ he said, glancing at the gray fields sliding past the window, "but the quiet is the part I will miss."
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: Teodor's words are a single quoted sentence interrupted by "he said, glancing at the gray fields sliding past the window." The first part of the quotation must end with a comma to separate it from the words that identify the speaker, and in American English that comma goes inside the closing quotation mark.
explanation.A: Incorrect. In American English, a comma that ends a quoted phrase goes inside the closing quotation mark, not outside it.
explanation.B: Correct. The comma separates the quotation from "he said," and it is placed inside the closing quotation mark, as American English requires.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A comma is needed to separate the quoted words from "he said"; without it, the quotation runs into the rest of the sentence.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate a quotation from the words that identify its speaker; a semicolon belongs only between independent clauses.
